la:pron:is.html:
is, ĕa, id (m. eis, C. I. L. 1, 198; n. it, , and freq. in MSS. of Plaut.),
gen. ējus (old form eiius, C. I. L. 3, 1365 et saep.; v. ; also etius,; scanned ĕius,; ; v. Lachm. ad ; also Cic. poët. N. D. 2, 42, 109: eius, monosyl.,; et saep.; dat. ĕï, in ante-class. poetry often ēi, ; ; ; : eiei, C. I. L. 1, 198, 12 al.: eei,: iei, C. I. L. 1, 205, col. 2, 12 al.: ei, monosyl.,; et saep.; ; cf. ; Lachm. ad : eo,; f. eae, Ritschl; ; v. ; acc. im for eum, Lex ap. ; ; Paul. ex ; also em, Tab. XII., tab. 1, fr. 1.— Plur. nom. m. ĕi, ; ; ; but in the MSS. ii; et saep.: eei,: iei, C. I. L. 1, 185; ; but ī,; ; v. Ritschl prol. p. 98; gen. eum for eorum, ; dat. and abl. eīs or iīs, also īs, C. I. L. 1, 198, 48; , and freq. in MSS.: eis, monosyl.,; ; v. Lachm. ad : ieis, C. I. L. 1, 204, col. 1, 5 al.; old form also ībus,; : ĭbus, Titin. et Pomp. ap. ; ; cf. S. C. ap. ; v. Lachm. l. l.; f. eābus, ; cf. ; v. more on these forms, Neue, Formenl. 2, 191-196), pron. demonstr. [root i-; Sanscr. itas; hence, i-ha, here; cf. i-bi, i-ta, i-dem, etc.].
He, she, it; this or that man, woman, thing.
Referring to something already mentioned, in gen.
Referring to the third person: fuit quidam senex Mercator: navem is fregit apud Andrum insulam: Is obiit mortem,: venit mihi obviam tuus puer: is mihi litteras abs te reddidit,: objecit ut probrum nobiliori, quod is, etc.,.—
Of the first person: ego me credidi Homini docto rem mandare: is lapidi mando maxumo,: haec omnia is feci, qui sodalis Dolabellae eram,; —
Of the second person: qui magister equitum fuisse tibi viderere, is per municipia cucurristi,.—
Esp.
In connection with a noun: ea re, quia turpe sit, faciendum non esse,: ea res ut est Helvetiis enuntiata, etc.,: ne ob eam rem tribueret, etc.,: flumen est Arar ... id flumen, etc.,: sub id tempus, Liv.

43, 5: ejus disputationis sententias memoriae mandavi,: ante eam diem,: ea tempestate,: quam urbem is rex condidit,.—

When is, ea, id would stand in the same case with the relative it is usually omitted; when the relative precedes, it is sometimes employed for emphasis: male se res habet, cum, quod virtute effici debet, id temptatur pecuniā,. —
Connected with que and quidem, it gives prominence to a preceding idea: cum una legione eaque vacillante,and that,: inprimis nobis sermo isque multus de te fuit,: tuus dolor humanus is quidem, sed, etc.,: vincula et ea sempiterna,: certa flagitiis merces, nec ea parva,.—
It is sometimes used instead of the reflexive pronoun: Helvetii persuadent Rauracis, ut una cum iis (for secum) proficiscantur,: Caesar etiam privatas injurias ultus est, quod ejus soceri avum Tigurini interfecerant,. —
It is sometimes placed, for greater emphasis, after a relative: multitudinem, quae fortunis vestris imminebat, eam ... se fecisse commemorat, ut, etc.,; cf.: urbem novam conditam vi et armis, jure eam legibusque de integro condere parat,.—
Id, n., to designate an idea in the most general manner, that (thing, fact, thought, circumstance, etc.).
In gen.: quando verba vana ad id locorum fuerint, rebus standum esse,hitherto, till now,; so, ad id (sc. tempus),: ad id diei,: ad id quod natura cogeret, i. e. death,: id temporis,at that time,; : : id aetatis,at that age,; cf. .—
Esp.
Id, therefore, for that reason, on that account: id ego gaudeo,: id misera maesta est,: idne estis auctores mihi?do you advise me to that?.—
Id genus = ejus generis, : aliquid id genus scribere,.—
Ad id, for that purpose: ad id quod sua quemque mala cogebant, evocati,: ad id quod = praeterquam quod, besides that: consul ad id, quod, etc., tunc quoque, etc.,; ; —
In id, to that end, on that account, therefore: in id fide a rege accepta,.—(ε) In eo est, it is gone so far, is at that pass: quod ad me de Lentulo scribis, non est in eo,it is not come to that, is not so,: cum jam in eo esset, ut in muros evaderet miles,when the soldiers were just on the point of scaling the walls,; ; : in eo est, also, it consists in that, depends upon that: totum in eo est tectorium, ut sit concinnum,: ejus omnis oratio versata est in eo, ut, etc.,: sic velim enitare quasi in eo mihi sint omnia,.— (ζ) Ex eo, from that, hence: sed tamen ex eo, quod eam voluptatem videtur amplexari saepe vehementius, etc.,. — (η) Cum eo, ut (with subj.), with the condition or stipulation that, etc., .— (θ) Eo, adverbially, with the comp., so much, by so much; but frequently to be expressed in English by the, ; so .—
Sometimes is refers to the foll. substantive, instead of to the preceding relative: quae vectigalia locasset, ea rata locatio (for eorum),: ea libera conjectura est (for de hac re),: quae pars major erit, eo stabitur consilio (for ejus),: existit ea, quae gemma dicitur,.—Sometimes, for emphasis, it is placed before the relative quod, to represent a thought or clause: ratus, id quod negotium poscebat, Jugurtham venturum,; : sive ille hoc ingenio potuisset, sive, id quod constaret, Platonis studiosus audiendi fuisset,: si nos, id quod debet, nostra patria delectat,: si, id quod facile factu fuit, vi armisque superassem,; ; so, id quo,: id de quo,. — It is thus apparently pleonastic after substantives: Octavio Mamilio—is longe princeps Latini nominis erat ...—ei Mamilio filiam nuptum dat, : cultrum, quem habebat, eum defigit,; cf. .—It is rarely pleonastic after the relative: quod ne id facere posses, idcirco dixeram, dub. (B. and K. bracket id). —
He, she, it; that man or the man (woman, thing), the one, that one, as a correlative to qui: si is, qui erit adductus,: is mihi profecto servus spectatus satis, Cui dominus curae est,. And also in the first person: haec tibi scribo ... is, qui flevi,.—
Such, of such a sort, character, or quality: in eum jam rediit locum, ut, etc.,: neque enim tu is es, qui, quid sis, nescias,; : itaque ego is in illum sum, quem tu me esse vis,: is eram natus ... ut potuerim,.—Adj.: nec tamen eas cenas quaero, ut magnae reliquiae fiant,; : quae causae sunt ejus modi, ut de earum jure dubium esse non possit,: est enim credo is vir iste, ut civitatis nomen sua auctoritate sustineat,. —
Such, so great, of so high a degree: L. Mescinius ea mecum consuetudine conjunctus est, quod mihi quaestor fuit,.—Hence, advv.
ĕā (sc. parte, viā, etc.), on that side, by that way, there: quod eā proxime accedi poterat,: itinera muniit: effecit ut eā elephantus ornatus ire posset, quā antea, etc.,: postquam comperit, transitum eā non esse,; ; fin.; 26, 11 fin.; 27, 15 fin. al. —
ĕō, v. 2. eo.

la:adv:isti.gloss: this same, this very; those, etc.

la:pron:iste.html:
iste, a, ud,
gen. istīus (the poets often make the penult of the gen. short: istĭus,: istius, dissyl.,; — An old form of the gen. isti, with modi, Cato ap. P.; .— With affixed ce: istisce,; and in interrogations, cine: istoscine patrem aequum'st mores liberis largirier?.—Dat. isto, al.; dat. f. istae, .—Shortened form, ste, sta, stoc, etc.; v. ; Lachm. ad ), pron. demonstr. [compounded of two pronom. stems, i- (cf. is) and to-; Sanscr. -ta; cf. tam, tum], this, that (man, woman, thing), called the demonstr. of the second person, since it is especially used in reference to persons and things connected in place, relation, or thought, with the person addressed.
In gen.
That (person or thing) near to you (in place or thought), that of yours, that of which you speak or with which you are connected: si ista nobis cogitatio de triumpho injecta non esset,: istae minae,those threats of yours,: de istis rebus exspecto tuas litteras,those affairs of yours,: quid quod adventu tuo ista subsellia vacuefacta sunt,those seats where you are sitting,; : quae est ista praetura?that prætorship of yours,: quaevis mallem fuisset (causa), quam ista quam dicis,.—
So with pronom. of the second person: cum enim tuus iste Stoicus sapiens dixerit,: quid iste tuus vates donat?: iste vester (sapiens),: quae tua est ista vita,. —
With a general reference, that, this, the very, that particular (person or thing), he, she, it.
Alone, as pron.: illae quae cum isto cubant,: credis quod iste dicit,: haec quae ista elementa videantur,. —
With substt.: erat enim ab isto Aristotele, a cujus inventis, etc.,: ista divina studia,: ut jam ne istius quidem rei culpam sustineam,: nec enim ab isto officio abduci debui,.—
With other pronouns: istius ipsius in dicendo facultatis,: transeat idem iste sapiens ad rem publicam tuendam. : in eodem isto Aegyptio regno vitā privatus,. —
With the rel.: necesse est eam, quae suum corpus prodixerit turpissimae cupiditati, timere permultos. Quos istos? etc.,. —
In partic.
Like is in the sense of tantus and talis, such, of such a kind: quare cum ista sis auctoritate, etc.,: servi mei, si me isto pacto metuerent, ut te metuunt omnes, etc.,: homines ista auctoritate praediti, qua vos estis,: animo isto esse,: egon, quidquam cum istis factis tibi respondeam,.—
It freq. implies scorn or contempt: non erit ista amicitia, sed mercatura,; : iste otii et pacis hostis,: animi est ista mollities, non virtus, inopiam paulisper ferre non posse,: hic vestis cum isto squalore permutandus,; : tuus iste frater,: o isti, an urgent form of address, et saep.—
In the abl.: isto, for this reason, therefore: isto tu's pauper, quom nimis sancte piu's,.

senses: that of yours, that related to you, that beside you
la:pron:istic.html:
istic (not isthic), aec, oc, and uc,
pron. demonstr. [for iste-ce; v. Neue, Formenl. II. p. 211 sqq.], this same, this, the very (person or thing).
In gen.
Substantively: isne istic fuit, quem vendidisti?: quid istic narrat,; .—
With a subst., usually with special reference to the person addressed, that of yours, that mentioned by or related to you (cf. iste): istac lege filiam tuam sponden mihi dari?: cum istoc ornatu,: istic labor,: haud istoc modo solita se me ante appellare,as you now do,: istaec praeda,: istic servus,: Sos. Egone? Amph. Tu istic, you yourself, : quis istic est qui deos tam parvi pendit?: istaec miseria,: malum istoc,: istaec res,: circum istaec loca commorari,, C, 1.—
Esp., in neutr. sing. and plur.: si istuc ita est,: istuc quidem considerabo,: ergo istoc magis, quia vanilocu's, vapulabis,so much the more,: istoc vilius,: dicitur, quidem, istuc, inquit, a Cotta,: istuc fractum,: non posse istaec sic abire,.—With gen.: quid istuc est verbi?: istuc aeta tis homo,; .—
Esp., with the demonstr. particle ce, and in interrogations cine: istucine interminata sum hinc abiens tibi?. 1, 14; : istocine pacto me adjutas?: istaece ridicularia,.—Hence,

la:adv:istinc.html:
istinc, adv.
istim-ce; cf. hinc, illinc
,
from there, thence, i. e. from the place of the person addressed, or a place related to that person.
Lit., of place: istinc loquere, si quid vis: procul tamen audiam,: serva istas fores, ne tibi clam se subterducat istinc. : age alter istinc, alter hinc adsistite,: istinc excludere,:

qui istinc veniunt, : emanare,; . —

Transf., thereof, i. e. of that thing: memento dimidium istinc mihi de praeda dare,: neque ergo partem posco mihi istinc de istoc vidulo,.

la:adv:isto.html:
istō, adv.
iste
,
thither, with reference to the place where the person addressed is.
Lit., of place: do fidem, si omittis, isto me intro ituram, quo jubes,: isto venire,; : peream si minima causa est properandi isto mihi,; 10, 17, 2: isto usque penetrasse,.—
Transf., thereinto, in that thing: Trebatium meum, quod isto admisceas, nihil est,; v. iste.

to the point in a discourse that you have reached or mentioned
la:adv:istuc.html:
istuc, adv.
isto- (iste) ce
,
thither, esp. in reference to the place where the party addressed is: concedite istuc,: istuc eo quantum potest,: jam istuc ego revortar,; : dabam operam, ut istuc veniam ante quam plane ex animo tuo effluo,: istuc mens animusque Fert,: dum transferor istuc,.—
Transf., to that thing, to that subject in discourse, etc.: hoc quod coepi primum enarrem: Post istuc veniam,: scio: istuc ibam,.

la:noun:isthmus.gloss: a strip of land between two seas; an isthmus
senses: a strip of land between two seas; an isthmus
la:noun:isthmus.html:
Isthmus or -os, i, m., = Ἰσθμός,
a strip of land between two seas, an isthmus, ; .—
Esp., the Isthmus of Corinth, where the Isthmian games were celebrated, ; ; ; ; ; ; . —
Transf., poet., a strait, viz., the Dardanelles, (4, 22, 2).—
Derivv.
Isthmĭus, a, um, adj., = Ἴσθμιος,of or belonging to the Isthmus, Isthmian: ludi,: labor,: Dione, i. e. Venus, who had a temple at Corinth, .—Esp. freq. subst.: Isthmĭa, ōrum, n., = τὰ Ἴσθμια,the Isthmian games, celebrated every five years at the Isthmus of Corinth, the victors in which received a pine garland, ; ; cf. .—
Isthmĭăcus (Isth-mĭcus), a, um, adj., of or belonging to the Isthmus, Isthmian: harena,: litus,: coloni, i. e. Syracusans (as a colony of Corinth), ; cf. favillae,.—Form Isthmicus, ; .

la:noun:isthmos.gloss: a strip of land between two seas; an isthmus

la:adv:istim.html:
istim, adv.
iste
,
thither, to that place (very rare): nolite, hospites, ad me adire! ilico istim! Enn. ap. ( Vahl., and Trag. Rel. v. 303 Rib., isti, in the same meaning): quod eos usque istim exauditos putem, (Klotz, but Baiter reads istinc): ite istim, ecferte lora, (acc. to Lachm. ad Lucr. vol. 2, p. 189; al. istinc).

la:noun:Ismarus.html:
Ismărus, i, m., or Ismăra, ōrum, n., = Ἴσμαρος,
a mountain on the southern coast of Thrace: Ismara propter,: juvat Ismara Baccho conserere,; .—Form Ismarus: Rhodope miratur et Ismarus Orphea,.—
Transf., the city at the foot of the mountain, and the territory belonging to it: quos Idas pater, et patria Ismara mittit,: Castra decem annorum, Ciconum manus, Ismara capta, (4, 11), 25.—
Derivv. Ismărĭ-cus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to Ismarus, Ismarian: Aquilo,. —
Ismărĭus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to Ismarus, Ismarian, Thracian: gentes,: juga,: Bacchae,: rex,i. e. Polymestor, king of Thrace,: vallis,the valley where Orpheus drew the wild beasts after him by the sound of his lyre, (3, 4, 6).
